annotations.shape: one message with NO MIME-Version and NO Content-Type whose body carries 8-bit non-ASCII bytes (0xE9 and 0xFF)
annotations.rfc_basis: RFC 2045 section 5.2: a part with no Content-Type header is text/plain; charset=us-ascii by default, but the body is not us-ascii. RFC 2045 section 5.2's default charset is us-ascii, so the bytes are not decodable as the default; the walker's charset ladder falls to windows-1252 and records that outcome. This label types the DECODE CHAIN the walker records (the point of the fixture) and leaves the decoded text open, because the fallback charset is the walker's choice, not the RFC's.
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was typed by a model from the RFC rules and read out of the fixture bytes (a byte/offset listing); never produced by running the library. labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person.
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, part.tree, part.gaps, decode.chain and body.content_sha256 -- the walker's existing decode-chain outcome for the undecodable-as-default bytes.
annotations.phase_1_facts: document.axes and body.selection (a displayable text view outside any group is n/a).
annotations.not_yet_labelled: headers.fields, part.regions and body.preamble_epilogue are not typed here; phases 2 and 3 are not exercised.

value: the RFC 2045 section 5.2 default charset is us-ascii, but the body is 8-bit and not us-ascii, so the decoded text is the walker's ladder outcome (windows-1252), not an RFC-determined string. This label records the decode chain and leaves the text open.
the quoting analysis runs over the decoded text, whose charset is the walker's fallback choice (see body.text); whether the fallback text has quote boundaries is left open rather than typed here.
